purpose: Retapamulin is a prescription antibiotic ointment used to treat small skin infections caused by certain bacteria, such as impetigo. It works directly on the skin where you apply it. It is only meant for skin use and should not be swallowed or used inside the body.
how_it_works: Retapamulin works by blocking the bacteria's ability to make the proteins they need to survive and grow. Without those proteins, the bacteria cannot multiply and eventually die off. This is a unique way of fighting bacteria that is different from many other antibiotics, which helps it work even against some hard-to-treat germs.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are mild and happen right where you apply the ointment. You might notice some redness, itching, burning, or a little swelling at the application site. These usually go away on their own and are not serious for most people.
warnings: Do not use this ointment in your eyes, nose, or mouth — it is for skin use only. If you develop a severe rash, hives, or have trouble breathing, stop using it and call your doctor right away, as this could be an allergic reaction. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, since certain drugs like ketoconazole can increase the amount of retapamulin in your body. Do not use it on large areas of broken or damaged skin without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is to apply a thin layer of the ointment to the affected skin area twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening — for 5 days. You can cover the area with a bandage if needed. Always wash your hands before and after applying. Finish the full 5 days even if the skin looks better sooner.
